newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Jet fuel slips, gas oil firms.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Jet fuel slips, gas oil firms.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps rose at midday on Thursday but jet fuel fell despite the recent spate of purchases by a local trader as market perception of declining seasonal demand overwhelmed the prompt support, traders said.
"Jet fuel is coming off as demand is entering a period of low demand," one trader said.
The April jet fuel/gas oil spread collapsed to trade earlier in the day at 35 cents per barrel down from an early week high of about $1.00, brokers said.
Traders said the fall in jet fuel prices was a reflection of market fundamentals as it enters a period of low demand after the peak winter season.
The fall came despite recent large purchases by a local trader who had since the start of last week bought a total of about one million barrels.

The latest being on Wednesday when the local trader bought two 100,000-barrel cargoes at $28.80 and $27.50 per barrel, loading March 27-April 1 and April 5-9, espectively, free-on-board (fob) Singapore.
Traders said the deals at 70-cents apart is a reflection of the steeply backwardated market where demand for the further out month is expected to be weak.

Similarly, the gas oil market is also developing a steep backwardation between the further out months of April and May, primarily due to the prompt demand from a local trader which was only on Tuesday extended to include April cargoes.
The local trader had until then bought only March cargoes which kept the March/April time spread at about $1.50 per barrel.
But currently the April/May time spread is also widening and was last quoted at $1.10/$1.20, a far cry from the 30-50 cents seen last week.
Outright April gas oil rose at midday to $25.20/$25.40 per barrel from Wednesday's $24.80/$24.90, brokers said.
The strength again was due to the same local trader who had since the start of last week bought around 2.2 two million barrels of gas oil.
On Wednesday the trader bought three cargoes totalling 520,000-barrels at between $28.00-26.45 per barrel, fob Singapore.
The prices again reflecting the steeply backwardated market.
March fuel oil swaps were down slightly in thin trading and was last quoted at $98.00/$99.50 per tonne from Wednesday's $98.50/$100.00.
